tasks.title: Python package, tooling and CLI skeleton
tasks.goal: An installable cottonwood package with an argparse CLI whose ruff, format, mypy and pytest checks pass through uv run.
tasks.plan:
1. Add pyproject.toml: project cottonwood, requires-python >=3.12, script cottonwood = cottonwood.cli:entry, hatchling build with packages [cottonwood], dev dependency group pytest/ruff/mypy, [tool.ruff] line-length 100 with lint select E,F,I,B,UP, [tool.mypy] strict with files cottonwood and tests, [tool.pytest.ini_options] testpaths tests, [tool.uv] cache-dir .uv-cache.
2. Add .python-version (3.12) and extend .gitignore with .venv/, .uv-cache/, __pycache__/, .pytest_cache/, .mypy_cache/, .ruff_cache/, dist/, data/, out/, *.db, *.sqlite3.
3. Add cottonwood/__init__.py (__version__), cottonwood/__main__.py, cottonwood/cli.py with build_parser() using required subparsers, main(argv) -> int that turns argparse SystemExit into its code, and entry() calling sys.exit(main()). Register a placeholder-free subcommand table so later commands plug in.
4. Add tests/test_cli.py: --help returns 0 and lists the program; no subcommand and an unknown subcommand return 2; main returns an int.
5. Run uv lock / uv sync and commit uv.lock; run all four checks.
acceptance_criteria: `uv run cottonwood --help` exits 0 and its output contains `cottonwood`.
`uv run cottonwood` with no subcommand and `uv run cottonwood not-a-command` each exit with code 2.
`cottonwood.cli.main([...])` returns the exit code as an int and a test in tests/test_cli.py asserts it.
`uv run mypy` exits 0 with `strict = true` in pyproject.toml's [tool.mypy] and both `cottonwood` and `tests` checked.
pyproject.toml holds the ruff, mypy and pytest configuration, and uv.lock exists in the repo.

tasks.title: Migrations runner and migrate command
tasks.goal: `cottonwood migrate` creates or upgrades a SQLite file through ordered NNN_*.sql migrations tracked with PRAGMA user_version.
tasks.plan:
1. Add db/migrations/001_baseline.sql (comment only, creates no tables).
2. Add cottonwood/db.py: MIGRATIONS_DIR (repo db/migrations), default_db_path() reading COTTONWOOD_DB else data/cottonwood.db, discover_migrations(dir) returning (number, path) sorted and rejecting duplicate numbers, migrate(db_path, migrations_dir) applying each migration with number > user_version in its own transaction and setting user_version, returning (from_version, to_version). Raise a clear error when the parent folder is missing, before connecting.
3. Add the migrate subcommand in cottonwood/cli.py with --db; print the version line; return 1 with `error: folder does not exist: <dir>` on a missing folder.
4. Add tests/test_migrate.py: fresh file at version 1 with no tables; second run applies nothing; two temp migrations applied in order; missing folder exits 1, names it and creates nothing; COTTONWOOD_DB and the data/cottonwood.db default; the CLI lists migrate in --help.
5. Run all four checks.
acceptance_criteria: `uv run cottonwood migrate --db` pointed at a path that does not exist yet exits 0 and creates a SQLite file whose `PRAGMA user_version` is 1 and whose sqlite_master has no rows for tables other than names starting with `sqlite_`.
Running migrate a second time on the same file exits 0 and leaves user_version unchanged, and a test asserts it.

A test with a temporary migrations directory holding two NNN_*.sql files shows both applied in numeric order and user_version set to the higher number; a file whose number is <= the current user_version is not applied.
When the --db parent folder does not exist, migrate exits 1, prints a message containing that folder path, and creates no file; a test asserts all three.
Without --db, migrate uses COTTONWOOD_DB when set and data/cottonwood.db otherwise, each shown by a test; `git check-ignore data/cottonwood.db` succeeds.
`uv run pytest` exits 0 and includes tests in both tests/test_cli.py and tests/test_migrate.py.
`uv run ruff check`, `uv run ruff format --check` and `uv run mypy` exit 0.
